rationale: Every illustration must feel 'sangar': dangerous, imposing or awe-inspiring, with the being as the undeniable subject. The owner rejected earlier images that read as an ordinary person, an ordinary animal, an empty landscape, or a calm, cute or decorative portrait. Those outcomes are failures regardless of technical quality.
prompt: ONE original square premium painterly cinematic Mitoloka illustration of Greiss, the Alpine cattle-killing demon in its documented black-cat guise. ANATOMY: one natural-sized black cat with one head, two natural feline eyes, four legs, one tail, no horns or luminous eyes; a far larger silver-white bull with normal bovine anatomy and nose ring facing it; a distant fully clothed maiden holding the bull's lead. MOMENT: Leap with arched back and bared teeth directly toward the charging silver-white bull's face, foreclaws extended, bull lowering horns to defeat the demon; tight close profile of malicious cat dominates foreground, clearly violent showdown rather than pet play. POWER: Documented demon confronted by the silver-white bull led uphill by maiden; no disease fog, dying animals, magical eyes or powers invented. SCALE & CAMERA: extreme low close angle; subject fills frame, natural documented size, never unsupported gigantic. LIGHT & WEATHER: one warm lateral source, deep shadows, crisp rim, physically moving dust/water only. SURFACE: tactile coarse textures, rich walnut/antique-gold palette. SETTING: Alpine pasture at Surenenalp with dark alpine roses and stormy mountain silhouettes. MOOD: dangerous or awe-inspiring, never ordinary, cute, calm or decorative. HARD CONSTRAINTS: no text, lettering, symbols, logos, border, signature, watermark; no extra heads or limbs; no franchises; no nudity, transparent clothes, blood, wounds or explicit gore; no generic glow aura, neon lines or energy ribbons.
